findings.text: nodemask_t is a fixed capacity container with one membership bit per NUMA node, sized by MAX_NUMNODES. Public helpers accept masks by value and forward the address plus a bit count to internal helpers. Raw word access is exposed for parsing and diagnostics.

Capacity and sentinel facts: MAX_NUMNODES is one shifted by NODES_SHIFT, with shift zero in single node configuration. NUMA_NO_NODE and NUMA_NO_MEMBLK are negative one sentinels. NR_NODE_MEMBLKS is twice MAX_NUMNODES. PAGE_COUNTER_MAX is LONG_MAX in one configuration and LONG_MAX scaled by page size in the other. Node state enumeration ends at NR_NODE_STATES.

Node mask mutation interface provides single bit set and clear plus whole mask fill with ones and fill with zeroes. Single bit helpers accept a volatile destination, whole mask helpers take an explicit length. Behavior is assignment of membership state, not reference counting.

Node mask query interface tests membership, atomically tests and sets one member, and evaluates whole mask relations: intersection, union, exclusive difference, difference, copy, complement, equality, overlap, subset, emptiness, fullness, and population count. Intersection and difference report whether the result is non empty; equality, overlap, subset, empty and full report truth values.

Node mask search and construction interface finds first set member, successor of a given member, wrapped successor that restarts at the beginning, and first clear member. It also builds a singleton mask for one node, either through a direct word store when the mask fits in one word or through clear plus set otherwise, and provides all-ones and all-zeroes constant masks plus iteration over set members.

Node mask conversion interface parses user memory and kernel list text into a mask, maps one bit position and whole masks from an old to a new numbering, projects an original mask through a relative map, and folds a mask by a stride. All forms take explicit destination and source masks with a length limit and report status where parsing is involved.

Search results are clamped so out of range outcomes collapse to MAX_NUMNODES as the not found sentinel. Wrapped successor returns the first member when no successor exists. Constant all-ones masks only set valid low bits in the final word via a last word mask. Single node iteration degenerates to at most one visit guarded by non emptiness.

Node state enumeration distinguishes possible, online, normal memory, high memory, any memory, CPU equipped, and generic initiator equipped nodes. High memory aliases normal memory when high memory support is absent. The enumeration size is bounded by a terminal count.

Per state membership accessors test, set, clear, and count nodes in a given state through a global table indexed by state. In single node configuration test reduces to identity against node zero, set and clear are no operations, and count is constantly one.

Online and memory convenience layer exposes first and next online and memory nodes, marks a node online or offline while refreshing the global online count, defines aliases for online and possible maps and their counts, tests possibility, picks a random set member with absent sentinel handling, and iterates over possible, online, and CPU equipped nodes.

Single node configuration fixes first online and first memory node to zero and makes next queries immediately report the end sentinel. Online and offline transitions become direct state set and clear without separate count maintenance in that configuration. Random selection returns zero without consulting the mask.

Temporary mask allocation has two configurations: heap allocation with paired release, or on stack object with no operation release. A scratch container bundles two masks and is allocated with non retry kernel memory semantics.
Scratch container layout holds exactly two node masks as first and second fields for algorithms needing a pair of temporaries.

NUMA helpers validate that an identifier lies within range zero inclusive to MAX_NUMNODES exclusive. Fallback nearest node queries report the absent sentinel regardless of input. Physical address to node mapping reports node zero and offline node data allocation is a no operation. Online node mapping is defined as nearest query constrained to online state. Section annotation for boot data is empty in one configuration and initial segment annotated in the other.
NUMA block discovery layout uses a block record with start address, end address, and owning node identifier, plus a table holding a block count and a fixed array of NR_NODE_MEMBLKS block records.

NUMA emulation fallback does nothing for table construction and reports invalid argument for command line parsing. Target node and address to node symbols are defined as self mapped macros in this configuration.

Out of memory classification enumerates no constraint, cpuset constraint, memory policy constraint, and memory cgroup constraint. Control record carries zonelist, policy mask pointer, target cgroup pointer, allocation mask, order where negative one denotes operator requested kill, total pages, chosen victim and score, and the deduced constraint.

Out of memory origin tracking sets, clears, and tests an origin flag on signal state, and victim testing inspects whether a task has an out of memory memory descriptor. Stable address space check returns a bus fault when the unstable descriptor flag is set and success otherwise.

Page counter layout tracks atomic usage, legacy failure count, effective and configured minimum and low protections with per counter and children usage, high and max limits, current and local watermarks, read mostly separation through padding and cache alignment, protection support and failure counting flags, and a parent pointer forming a hierarchy.

Page counter operations initialize usage to zero, limit to maximum, parent linkage, protection mode, and disabled failure counting; publish the high limit with ordered store semantics; reset both watermarks to current usage with local value written first; and provide a no operation protection recalculation entry in this configuration.
Page counter watermark reset preserves the ordering property that the local watermark never observes a newer usage value than the shared watermark apart from hardware or compiler reordering.

Page extension framework layouts: operations record with byte offset, byte size, presence predicate, one time initializer, and shared flags need; flags enumeration for owner tracking, allocated state, and young plus idle states on narrow configurations with idle support; per page record holding flags; iterator holding index, start frame number, and current record pointer.

Page extension lifecycle in these fragments reports early enablement from a global flag and provides empty initializers for flat memory setup and general setup. Data access adds the operation offset to the record base and record advance adds the global record stride.

Page extension iteration over a frame range starts by rejecting empty counts, recording zero index and start frame, and resolving the first record. Each step warns once and stops on missing current record, stops when the index reaches the count, otherwise resolves the next frame by pointer stride on fast path frames and by fresh lookup when crossing allocation granularity, and exposes the current record through a getter and a loop macro.

Fast record advance is permitted for every frame in one configuration and only when the frame number is not at an allocation section boundary in the other, requiring lookup at boundaries because backing storage is section based.

membership updates use distinct atomic versus plain primitives, so only the explicit test and set form returns prior state atomically. Singleton construction shifts by caller supplied node number, so callers must keep it below word width in the direct word path. User text and list parsing can fail and remap style transforms depend on caller supplied map validity. Iterator relies on fresh lookup at section boundaries.
